statement: Conditional overlap-to-excess lemma. Let k composable systems have excesses e_1,...,e_k and successive overlap subspaces U_1,...,U_{k-1}, with the T52 composition law applying at every composition. If e_i >= a for all i and sum_i dim(U_i) <= b k, then total excess e^* >= k(a-2b). Thus a > 2b implies linear excess in k.
proof: Induct on k using the composition law at each step. Each composition adds the next component excess and subtracts twice the dimension of that step's overlap, so e^* = sum_i e_i - 2 sum_i dim(U_i). The assumptions give sum_i e_i >= ka and 2 sum_i dim(U_i) <= 2bk. Hence e^* >= ka-2bk = k(a-2b), which is linear and positive when a>2b.

proved_step:
statement: Composition-tree excess identity and sufficient margin. Let T be any finite rooted binary tree whose leaves are component systems with excesses e_i, and whose internal nodes v compose their two children under the exact law e(v)=e(v_L)+e(v_R)-2d_v, where d_v=dim(U_v) is the overlap dimension at v. Then e(root)=sum_i e_i-2 sum_{v internal} d_v. In particular, for any parameter s>0, if sum_i e_i>=a s and sum_{v internal}d_v<=b s, then e(root)>=(a-2b)s; hence a>2b gives linear excess in s.
proof: Induct on the number of leaves. A one-leaf tree has root excess e_1 and an empty internal-node sum, so the identity holds. For a tree with at least two leaves, apply the induction hypothesis to the two child subtrees: their root excesses equal the sums of their respective leaf excesses minus twice their respective internal overlap sums. The root composition law adds those two expressions and subtracts 2d_root. The leaf sets and internal nodes of the two subtrees, together with the root, partition the leaves and internal nodes of T, giving the stated identity. Under the two inequalities, substitute into the identity to obtain e(root)>=as-2bs=(a-2b)s. If a>2b this lower bound is positive and proportional to s.

proved_step:
statement: Overlap-budget lemma for a composition tree. Let T be a finite rooted binary tree with q leaves and internal overlap dimensions d_v >= 0. Suppose every internal node obeys e(v)=e(v_L)+e(v_R)-2d_v, every leaf has excess e_i >= a, and every internal overlap satisfies d_v <= delta. Then e(root) >= qa - 2delta(q-1). In particular, if a > 2delta, then e(root) >= q(a-2delta)+2delta.
proof: Inductively expanding the local composition law gives e(root)=sum_i e_i-2sum_v d_v. A finite full binary tree with q leaves has q-1 internal nodes: this follows by induction, since joining subtrees with q_L and q_R leaves gives 1+(q_L-1)+(q_R-1)=q-1 internal nodes. Therefore sum_i e_i >= qa and sum_v d_v <= delta(q-1), so e(root) >= qa-2delta(q-1) = q(a-2delta)+2delta.
